union.text: the Don, the Kuban (Ekaterinodar) and the North Caucasus: the territory the Volunteer Army and the Cossack hosts held when South Russia was set up on 8 January 1919

correction.text: at the October 1919 peak: "Ukraine, Crimea, Kuban, the North Caucasus" with the Black Earth region, the Lower Volga and the Don region; Denikin's forces within 350 km of Moscow

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the shape at the October 1919 peak. The pages give no area; the page lists "Ukraine, Crimea, Kuban, the North Caucasus" plus the Black Earth region, Lower Volga and Don. Oblasts are the researcher's reading of those names; the ledger takes Donbas, Kharkov, Tsaritsyn, Kiev, Kursk, Voronezh and Orel in during 1919 and the Red Army takes Orel, Voronezh, Kursk (October-November) and Kharkov (December) out again within the year. Cliopatria's Russian Republic shape (17.9-18.6 M km2 for 1918-1919) covers all of it.

correction.text: "the Crimean Peninsula and adjacent areas of the mainland": the former Taurida Governorate, with Northern Taurida (Melitopol, Henichesk) until the Red offensive of 28 October 1920

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the longest part of 1920 (April to November): Wrangel's Government of South Russia, "the Crimean Peninsula and adjacent areas of the mainland". Until April the Don, Kuban and North Caucasus were still held (ledger: Rostov 3-10 January, Novorossiysk 26-27 March, Kuban Army surrender 18-20 April). The page gives no area.

region.text: the Don, the Kuban (Ekaterinodar) and the North Caucasus: the territory the Volunteer Army and the Cossack hosts held when South Russia was set up on 8 January 1919

ledger.note: 1919, 8 January: South Russia is established by the White movement on the Don, the Kuban and the North Caucasus, under Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia. "South Russia was established on 8 January 1919 by the White movement": the page lists the territory as Ukraine, Crimea, Kuban and the North Caucasus without dates; the founding core is the researcher's reading from the Denikin page (Ekaterinodar taken August 1918, a Don base by May 1918).

1919, May: the AFSR offensive forces the Red Southern Front to retreat; the Denikin page adds that in spring 1919 his forces "checked a major Red offensive in the Donbas region" and in May "a series of counter-offensives routed the Red armies". The pages give no day for the Donbas; region and month are the researcher's reading. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: split from the former Kharkov-and-Donbas event; Kharkov now has its own dated event.]

1919, May: the AFSR offensive "forced the front to retreat from" Kharkov, Belgorod, Balashov and Tsaritsyn (the page gives no day for any of them). Belgorod is Russian land, so the counterpart is the RSFSR; Balashov lies outside this dossier's shape. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: Belgorod was lumped with Kharkov and the Donbas against the Ukrainian SSR.]

region.text: the Southern Front between the Armed Forces of South Russia and the Red Army, 1919-1920

ledger.note: 1919, May: the Southern Front opens along the Donbas and Kharkov as Denikin's counter-offensives rout the Red armies; zone drawn from the cities and regions the pages name (the Kursk-Orel-Voronezh belt, Donbas, Tsaritsyn).

1919, June: "In June 1919, after a fierce battle, Wrangel's troops stormed and captured the heavily fortified city" (Tsaritsyn, now Volgograd). The Southern Front page puts the retreat from Tsaritsyn in the May offensive without a day; the Armed Forces of South Russia page has Denikin welcomed in Tsaritsyn on 1 July 1919. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: split out of the former /ledger/0 ("Tsaritsyn, Kiev and Kursk", year only, set against the Ukrainian SSR). Tsaritsyn was RSFSR land; the Wrangel page dates the capture to June 1919.]

1919, 25 June: "On 25 June 1919, Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia captured Kharkov, followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June." The Southern Front page says only that the May offensive forced the front to leave Kharkov. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the earlier May date was the offensive's month; the Ukrainian War of Independence page dates the capture.]

1919, 30 June: Denikin's forces captured Kharkov on 25 June, "followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June" (Yekaterinoslav, now Dnipro). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: dated capture split out of the former undated Ukrainian-oblasts event.]

1919, 31 July: "He took Poltava on July 31, Odesa on August 23, and Kyiv on August 31" (Kenez, quoted on the page). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: dated capture split out of the former undated Ukrainian-oblasts event.]

1919, 23 August: Denikin "took ... Odesa on August 23" (Kenez, quoted on the page); the Southern Front page lists Odessa among the cities the front gave up between August and October. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: dated capture split out of the former undated Ukrainian-oblasts event.]

1919, 31 August: "... and Kyiv on August 31" (Kenez, quoted on the page); the Ukrainian-Soviet War page agrees ("on 31 August Anton Denikin's Volunteer Army established its positions in the city"), and the Southern Front page puts the front's loss of Kiev between August and October. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: split out of the former /ledger/0, which had only the year; Kiev was Ukrainian SSR land.]

1919, September: the Southern Front gave up "Kiev, Odessa, Kursk, Voronezh, and Orel between August and October" and "through September and early October the front retreated to the north again", Kursk being lost in that retreat; the page gives no day (the Orel-Kursk operation of 11 October-18 November retakes it). Month is the researcher's reading of the window. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: split out of the former /ledger/0; Kursk was RSFSR land, not Ukrainian SSR land.]
1919, 30 September: "on 30 September, Voronezh and Orel": the Whites take both; by October they are within 350 km of Moscow, South Russia's greatest extent.

region.text: the rest of the Ukrainian lands at the October 1919 peak (Kiev Oblast outside the city)

ledger.note: 1919, autumn: the remaining Ukrainian oblasts are inside the territory at the peak. Bridging: the South Russia page lists "Ukraine" without dating the captures or naming oblasts, the Southern Front page does not mention them, and the Ukrainian War of Independence and Armed Forces of South Russia pages date only Kharkov, Yekaterinoslav, Poltava, Odesa and Kyiv (now separate events); the Moscow Directive page suggested by the reviewer returns url_not_found. The oblast list is the researcher's reading. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the dated cities were split out; the rest stays at confidence 1.]

1919, 11 October to 18 November: the Red Southern Front retakes Orel, Kursk (Orel-Kursk operation) and Voronezh (13 October to 16 November). The pages give the operations' spans, not the days; "decisively defeated ... at Orel and Voronezh" in late October (Denikin page). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: Belgorod moved to its own December event, dated by the Kharkov operation.]

1919, 24 November to 12 December: the Red Southern Front takes Kharkov, Sumy, Belgorod and Stary Oskol (Kharkov operation; the page gives day and month without a year). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: Belgorod, Russian land, moved to its own event against the RSFSR.]

1919, 24 November to 12 December: the Red Southern Front takes Kharkov, Belgorod and Stary Oskol in the Kharkov operation (the page gives day and month without a year). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: split from the former Kharkov-Sumy-Belgorod event, whose counterpart was the Ukrainian SSR.]
1920, 3-10 January: the Red Southern Front takes Taganrog, Novocherkassk, Rostov-on-Don and Tikhoretsk and reaches the Sea of Azov (Rostov-Novocherkassk operation; day and month only on the page).

region.text: the rest of the Don Oblast and the Lower Volga

ledger.note: 1920, January: the Southern Front "pushed the Armed Forces of South Russia back to the Black Sea and North Caucasus by early 1920" (the Rostov-Novocherkassk operation, 3-10 January; the front was renamed the South-Western Front on 10 January 1920). The page does not date the fall of Tsaritsyn (Volgograd) or the rest of the Don; bridging. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: split out of the former /ledger/9, which had set these Russian oblasts against the Ukrainian SSR.]

1920, winter: the rest of Ukraine falls to the Reds: "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands" (Ukrainian War of Independence page). Bridging: no page opened dates Kiev, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav or Odessa (the Ukrainian War of Independence, Armed Forces of South Russia and Southern Front pages are silent; the AFSR page lists "Battle of Kiev (December 1919)" and "Odessa Operation (1920)" without days). Dated to the January-March 1920 collapse between Rostov (3-10 January) and Novorossiysk (March). [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: Rostov and Volgograd oblasts moved to their own event against the RSFSR; source changed to the page that dates 1920.]

region.text: Novorossiysk and the Black Sea coast

ledger.note: 1920, 26-27 March: the Volunteer Army's remaining troops are evacuated from Novorossiysk to the Crimea.
1920, late March: the Southern Front ends on the mainland with the evacuation from Novorossiysk; only the Kuban Army (to April) and the Crimea remain.

1920, 4 April: the Government of South Russia is established (infobox "Established: 4 April 1920") in Sevastopol, successor to Denikin's South Russian Government ("set up in February 1920"); it adopted the name "Government of South Russia" officially on 16 August 1920 and France recognised it in August 1920. The Armed Forces of South Russia page adds that in early April 1920 Denikin "delegated all authority to Pyotr Wrangel"; the state continues on the Crimea. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the earlier note said Denikin resigned in favour of Wrangel, who set up the government, which the Government of South Russia page does not say.]
1920, April: the capital moves to Sevastopol (infobox of the Government of South Russia); the South Russia page says Wrangel "set up a new government in Sevastopol ... in April".

region.text: the Kuban and the North Caucasus

ledger.note: 1920, 18-20 April: the Kuban Army, which replaced the Caucasus Army on 29 January 1920, surrenders to the Red Army; the Kuban and the North Caucasus are lost.

1920, June: "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation" and "his forces broke out of the Crimean bottleneck and captured a large territory to the north" (Pyotr Wrangel page). The page names neither Melitopol nor Henichesk (the Southern Front page lists Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar among the places the Reds retook on 28 October-3 November) and the Government of South Russia page says only that the offensives there "failed". By modern boundaries Northern Taurida lies in Zaporizhzhya and Kherson oblasts, inside the Ukrainian SSR's shape and outside the RSFSR's, and no page says which republic administered it in 1920, so the counterpart is the Ukrainian SSR. Confidence 2: the page dates the offensive; the region is the researcher's reading. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: date June 1920 from the Wrangel page (was year-less bridging at confidence 1); counterpart changed from the RSFSR to the Ukrainian SSR so that the mirror exists in a dossier whose shape holds the land.]

1920, 28 October: the Red Southern Front advances out of the Kakhovka bridgehead into Northern Taurida (Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol, Chongar, 28 October to 3 November), then through Perekop and Chongar (7-17 November).

1920, 28 October to 3 November: the Red Southern Front's "counteroffensive in northern Taurida between 28 October and 3 November" captured Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar; the Perekop-Chongar operation followed on 7-17 November. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the Northern Taurida loss had no event; mirrors the gain of June 1920.]

1920, 7-17 November: "Between 7 and 17 November it broke through Russian Army defenses on the Isthmus of Perekop" (the Lithuanian Peninsula, the Turkish Wall, Yushun and the Chongar positions), and Wrangel "initiated an evacuation of 146,000 people to Constantinople with the last boats departing on 16 November". The Southern Front page, cited here as a second page, says the Perekop-Chongar operation (7-17 November) then captured Simferopol, Feodosiya, Sevastopol, Kerch and Yalta. [eu-17-x repair 2026-10-25: the earlier note put the Sivash crossing and that list of towns on the Government of South Russia page, which does not name them.]
1920, 17 November: the fighting for Northern Taurida and the Crimea ends.
1920, 17 November: the Government of South Russia is dissolved after the loss of the Crimea; South Russia ends.

wars.name: Southern Front (Russian Civil War)

zones.text: Donbas, Kharkov, the Kursk-Orel-Voronezh belt and Tsaritsyn, 1919-1920

wars.outcome: Red victory: Orel, Kursk and Voronezh retaken October-November 1919, Kharkov December 1919, Rostov January 1920, Novorossiysk March 1920, the Kuban April 1920.
wars.note: The Southern Front page gives day and month without a year for each operation; the 1919-1920 sequence is the one the Denikin page supports.

wars.name: Siege of Perekop
wars.outcome: Red victory: Perekop and Chongar broken 7-17 November 1920; evacuation of 146,000 people from Sevastopol to Constantinople by 16 November.
wars.note: The South Russia page names it "the Siege of Perekop in November 1920"; the Southern Front page calls the operation Perekop-Chongar (7-17 November).

certainty.note: Civil-war fronts and cities, not lines; the oblasts are readings from the names on the pages. The Crimean isthmus (Perekop-Chongar) is a firm line.

sources.note: Kenez, quoted: "He took Poltava on July 31, Odesa on August 23, and Kyiv on August 31"; "On 25 June 1919, ... captured Kharkov, followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June"; "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands"; silent on Kyiv, Poltava, Odesa in Dec 1919-Feb 1920.

sources.title: Pyotr Wrangel
sources.note: "In June 1919 ... Wrangel's troops stormed and captured" Tsaritsyn; "On 4 April [1920] a military council elected Wrangel"; "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation"; no Melitopol.

notes: No Cliopatria row; Cliopatria's Russian Republic shapes (1917-1919) and Republics of the Soviet Union (1920-1921) cover all of this land. The pages are thin on territory: no page opened gives an area, the capital moves only in infobox form, and the oblast lists are readings of "Ukraine, Crimea, Kuban, the North Caucasus, the Black Earth region, the Lower Volga, the Don". Not settled: the captures of Kiev, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav and Odessa (undated on these pages; confidence 1 events), the Terek and Dagestan (not named), the Don Republic and the Kuban Rada as separate Cossack governments (not on the pages), and Ukrainian People's Republic claims in 1919 (appears only in the South Russia page's succession table). One dossier for Denikin's South Russia and Wrangel's Government of South Russia (Wikipedia lists the second as a state succeeding the first; treated as a government change on the same state). Gazetteer: Henichesk is missing (used a radius around 34.82E 46.17N). Counterpart states needing dossiers: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic (this batch), Crimean ASSR, the Don Republic and the Kuban People's Republic. Repair 2026-10-25 (eu-17-x-fixed, after the reviewer's fail): the former /ledger/0 (Tsaritsyn, Kiev and Kursk, year only, sorted before the January 1919 founding) is split into Tsaritsyn (June 1919, RSFSR, Wrangel page), Kiev (31 August 1919, Ukrainian SSR) and Kursk (September 1919, RSFSR, confidence 2); Kharkov moved to 25 June 1919 (Ukrainian War of Independence page; the Southern Front page gives only the May offensive) and Yekaterinoslav, Poltava, Odesa and Kiev are dated 30 June, 31 July, 23 August and 31 August 1919; the undated rest of Ukraine stays at confidence 1; the winter 1920 loss stays at confidence 1 because the Ukrainian War of Independence, Armed Forces of South Russia and Southern Front pages are silent on Kiev, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav and Odessa (the Moscow Directive page is url_not_found, also as 'Moscow_directive'); Northern Taurida is June 1920 (Wrangel page) and its counterpart is now the Ukrainian SSR (the land is inside that shape, not the RSFSR's), with a new loss on 28 October-3 November 1920; Belgorod and the Rostov-Volgograd remainder are set against the RSFSR, not the Ukrainian SSR; the rename and Crimea-loss notes are trimmed to what the Government of South Russia page says (4 April 1920 establishment; Perekop breakthrough 7-17 November; 146,000 evacuated; it does not name Simferopol to Yalta, which the Southern Front page does). The mirrors are added in the Ukrainian SSR and RSFSR dossiers of this batch.
